skill.name: cellxgene-census
skill.description: Use CZ CELLxGENE Census guidance to query single-cell metadata and expression data, filter by biology, and plan scanpy or PyTorch workflows.
skill.summary: Build reproducible CZ CELLxGENE Census queries for single-cell metadata, expression matrices, and downstream analysis workflows.

content.value_statement: Single-cell researchers need precise Census queries without loading excessive data. This skill guides metadata filtering, expression retrieval, batch processing, and scanpy or PyTorch integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to open stable or versioned Census releases.
Provides metadata filters for cell type, tissue, disease, donor, and genes.
Shows AnnData retrieval for small and medium expression queries.
Outlines out-of-core TileDB-SOMA workflows for large cell sets.
Describes scanpy and PyTorch integration patterns using Census data.
Highlights reproducibility practices such as version pinning and primary-data filters.
limitations: Does not execute Census queries or verify live dataset availability by itself.
Does not replace statistical review of experimental design or normalization choices.
Large queries still require local memory planning and appropriate compute resources.
Examples assume users install and configure the official cellxgene-census package.

use_cases.title: Explore tissue cell types
use_cases.description: Find available cell types, tissues, diseases, and dataset metadata before loading expression matrices.

use_cases.title: Prepare machine learning datasets
use_cases.description: Plan Census filters and PyTorch dataloaders for cell type classification or representation learning.

use_cases.title: Design reproducible analyses
use_cases.description: Use pinned Census versions, primary-data filters, and selected metadata columns for repeatable workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Survey a tissue
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me explore cell types available for lung tissue in CZ CELLxGENE Census. Include the safest metadata filters to start with.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve marker expression
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Census query for T cell marker genes in COVID-19 samples. Include cell, gene, and primary-data filters.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a large query
prompt_templates.prompt: I need brain data across several genes, but the result may be large. Show an out-of-core query strategy and size checks.

prompt_templates.title: Build an ML workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PyTorch workflow using Census data for cell type classification. Include versioning, train-test splitting, and batch handling.

output_examples.input: Explore immune cells in lung tissue.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend starting with metadata-only filters for lung tissue and primary data, then reviewing cell type counts.

output_examples.input: Query CD4 and CD8A expression in T cells.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline gene filtering, T cell observation filters, selected metadata columns, and AnnData retrieval considerations.
The skill would recommend estimating cell counts first, then using TileDB-SOMA batch iteration instead of loading all cells at once.

best_practices: Filter for primary data unless duplicate cells are part of the analysis.
Pin the Census version when results must be reproducible.
Estimate query size before loading expression matrices into memory.
anti_patterns: Loading broad Census queries directly into memory without checking cell counts.
Mixing Census versions within one analysis without documenting the change.
Requesting every metadata column when only a few fields are needed.

faq.question: What is CZ CELLxGENE Census?
faq.answer: It is a versioned collection of standardized single-cell data from CZ CELLxGENE Discover.

faq.question: Can this skill run the Census API for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for queries that you run in your own environment.

faq.question: Which organisms does the guidance cover?
faq.answer: The examples focus on human and mouse data, matching the Census organism structure.

faq.question: Why should I filter for primary data?
faq.answer: Primary-data filters help avoid duplicate cells when counting or comparing cells across datasets.

faq.question: Does it support scanpy workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes how Census AnnData outputs can feed common scanpy preprocessing and visualization steps.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
